Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Twyne (writing app, Convex backend) at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne, branch feat/clairic-extraction. Read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` first.

GOAL: make auto-research drivable through the personal-access-token integration API (`POST /api/integrations/v1`), so the eval harness in `evals/app/` can measure it the way it already measures the room, rubric, rewrites and interview. Implement the two operations in the "Auto-research" section of `docs/app-harness.md`: `research.targets` and `research.sources`. That section is the contract; another agent (Astra) is building the CLI against it right now, so keep the names and shapes, or tell me precisely what you changed and why.

They must run the same logic the product runs, not a reimplementation. The browser's background pass is `src/utils/background-research.ts`:
- hosted writers get `extractOnService`: `claimCandidates`, then a System One confirmation (`candidateRequest` / `confirmedTargets` in `src/utils/research-candidates.ts`);
- writers with their own model get `runClientResearchExtract` (`src/utils/ai-client.ts`), the research-extract prompts parsed by `parseResearchTargets`;
- search goes through `convex/research.ts` `searchSources`, with `buildResearchSearchContext` and `rankSourcesForTarget` from `src/utils/research-targets.ts`.

The model strategy runs those prompts on the hosted model (Not Organic or the legacy route via `pickProvider`). Hosted writers don't have this path today; the eval exists partly to compare the two strategies.

Existing patterns to follow (all from today):
- `HostedCaller` and `callerFromIdentity` / `callerFromTokenIdentifier` in `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts`.
- Public actions are split into a wrapper plus a `*Core(ctx, caller, args)`, with internal `*As` actions taking `ownerId` (see `convex/systemOne.ts` `askAs`, and the cores in `convex/agents.ts`).
- The token path dispatches through `convex/lib/integrationAiRequests.ts` to internal actions in `convex/integrationAi.ts`.
- Field errors use "is required" / "must be" messages; app errors use codes (e.g. 503 `configuration_required` when there is no live search provider, rather than placeholder results).
- `generateWithSecondChance` in agents.ts retries empty model output.

STATE YOU INHERIT: I had started `convex/research.ts`. It now has `searchSourcesCore` / `searchSourcesAs` (caller-based, same rate limits), plus a `RESEARCH_PROVIDER=notorganic` provider that searches Not Organic's metered `/v1/web/search` as the caller's linked DID, so hosted research needs no separate key. It is unfinished: `providerSearch` still has its old 2-argument signature, and the provider id plumbing doesn't know about "notorganic". Finish it or rework it as you see fit. Don't try to fix Not Organic itself: its prod gateway currently answers web search with 502, because of a stale upstream key on their side. Your code just has to handle failure gracefully.

TESTS: extend `convex/integrationAi.test.ts`. Its local stub server already answers `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/systemone`; a custom search provider (`RESEARCH_PROVIDER=custom` + `RESEARCH_SEARCH_URL`) can point at it too. Cover both strategies, sources, and the no-provider 503. Run only that file plus `convex/integrations.test.ts` (`npx vitest run …`), and tsc at most once. The full suite takes over 10 minutes, so don't run it.

CONSTRAINTS: shared checkout with other agents. Don't touch `evals/app/`, `packages/twyne-tools/`, or `prompts/`. No state-changing git, no deploy, no `convex dev`; codegen only if you add a module. Re-read files right before editing them.

Report: files changed, any contract deviations, how the notorganic provider behaves, test summary lines.
I’ll read the Convex guidelines and API contract, finish the shared research paths, wire the token operations, and run only the requested checks.

I’m applying the Convex expert skill for function structure and validators. Your explicit limits take precedence over its deployment steps: I won’t deploy, run `convex dev`, or touch the CLI and prompt directories.
